decision: SUPPORTS — all five frozen decision-rule conditions satisfied (C1-C5). Permission escalation discrimination 1.0, session invalidation discrimination 1.0, null control 0.0 with CI containing 0.0, full-vector >= max baseline, null control <= 0.05. However, claim ceiling is narrowed per audit: discrimination is deterministic (1 unique fingerprint per state, degenerate bootstrap CI), C4 is vacuous (full == body == status == 1.0 because status and body change simultaneously), and results are bounded to localhost Flask dev server with maximally-distinct writable controls. C-MEAS-VALID remains EXPERIMENTAL with expanded ceiling. C-FRESHNESS and C-DELTA-REPAIR unblocked for localhost synthetic testing but NOT for distributed production testing.

claim_updates.reason: All five frozen decision-rule conditions pass on localhost Flask+SQLite+JWT testbed: C1 permission_disc=1.0>0.5, C2 session_disc=1.0>0.5, C3 null=0.0 CI[0.0,0.0], C4 full>=max_baseline (vacuous equality 1.0>=1.0), C5 null<=0.05. C-MEAS-VALID advances from prior EXPERIMENTAL ceiling (nginx decompression) to include writable/auth/session/drift controls on localhost. The claim ceiling is: Flask 3.1.3 + PyJWT 2.14.0 + SQLite WAL on localhost 127.0.0.1:19847, SQLite-backed role lookup (role not in JWT), session validity via DELETE, deterministic responses (1 unique fingerprint per state), headers filtered (Date/Server/X-Request-Id excluded), N=20 per state, SEED=44. NOT VALIDATED because: (1) C4 is vacuous — body and status change simultaneously on both positive conditions, full vector cannot exceed single-field baselines at ceiling 1.0; (2) bootstrap CI is degenerate due to deterministic responses (effective N=1 per state); (3) same-status body-only permission change and header-only drift are untested; (4) production middleware, CDN, concurrent load, HTTP/2, TLS untested. C-FRESHNESS and C-DELTA-REPAIR unblocked for localhost synthetic measurement but NOT for distributed/production testing.

product_action: NO_CHANGE — C-MEAS-VALID remains EXPERIMENTAL. Writable/auth/session/drift controls demonstrated on localhost testbed. C-FRESHNESS and C-DELTA-REPAIR unblocked for localhost measurement substrate, not for distributed production infrastructure. No Product Core promotion warranted.
next_question: Does the HTTP fingerprint substrate discriminate when response bodies and status codes are identical but server-side state changes only independent headers (e.g., Cache-Control, ETag, Set-Cookie) — isolating header-only drift from body/status confounds?
reason: The frozen decision rule passes all five conditions, but the audit correctly identifies that the experiment demonstrates SQLite writes change HTTP responses (trivially, when status+body change simultaneously), not that the full-vector fingerprint adds marginal value beyond single-field baselines. C4 is vacuous (1.0>=1.0 equality). The next high-information question is whether the substrate can detect header-only drift where bodies are identical — this directly tests the substrate's utility for C-FRESHNESS (session/auth drift detection when response content is unchanged) and C-DELTA-REPAIR (perturbation measurement when only metadata varies). This is materially orthogonal to the current maximally-distinct design and addresses the audit's V2 (ceiling effect) and V3 (header correlation) findings.
